newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian instant coffee makers target middle-class.
newsitem.headline: Indian instant coffee makers target middle-class.

text.p: Instant coffee needs to become popular with India's growing middle-class to help boost stagnating domestic consumption, a leading coffee producer said on Thursday.
"We are campaigning among middle-class people to make them take up the habit of drinking coffee," said Rajendra Prasad, managing director of Continental Coffee Ltd.
He told reporters coffee was considered a drink of the rich and this notion had to be changed to make it acceptable to other classes.

"If coffee consumption has to grow it has to be instant coffee," Prasad said. Currently instant coffee accounted for only 8,000-10,000 tonnes out of a total consumption of 50,000-60,000 tonnes, he said.
Prasad said Indian coffees were used for blending as they were among the best in the world.
"Indian coffees are not only mountain-grown and hand-picked, as are the much-advertised Colombian varieties, but are also hand-graded, a fact which is not well-known," he said.
India's average annual coffee production is around 200,000 tonnes. It grows Arabica and Robusta coffees in equal measure, which gives flexibility to its products.
"We can give the product any taste the world needs," he said adding that quality control was the key to marketing. "The coffee world is small and reputation is very important."
In September last year India freed coffee trade from five decades of controls, allowing growers to directly market all their produce.
Coffee exports rose to 153,000 tonnes in 1995-96 (April-March) from 137,400 the previous year, their value moving up to 13.70 billion rupees from 11 billion in the same period.
Figures for instant coffee exports were not immediately available.
